caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
debt_management: Public debt is low by regional standards: 20.6% of GDP in 2006, a low of 18.2% in 2007, rising to 47.1% in 2014 after flood-related borrowing and IMF programs, then falling steadily to a projected 29.9% in 2025. COVID pushed it temporarily to 37.2% in 2020. GDP grew from $12.9bn in 2006 to a projected $33.0bn in 2025. The currency-board regime and IMF anchors have kept fiscal policy conservative; debt sustainability is not a binding constraint.
inflation_management: The currency board pegging the convertible mark to the euro makes Bosnia an importer of euro-area monetary conditions. Inflation was near zero or negative through the mid-2010s (-1.6% in 2016, the series low) as euro-area disinflation spilled over. The 2022 shock hit hard: 14%, the series high, on energy and food imports. Disinflation was quick — 1.7% by 2024 — with a projected 3.9% for 2025. The board precludes active monetary management; adjustment runs through wages and prices.

key_events.event: Currency board provided stability during the global financial crisis; growth slowed sharply but the peg held.
Devastating floods and IMF programs pushed debt to 47.1% of GDP, the series high.
Deflationary episode bottomed at -1.6% amid weak euro-area spillovers.
COVID-19: debt rose to 37.2% of GDP on the economic contraction.
Inflation spiked to 14% on imported energy and food prices.
EU candidate status (granted December 2022) anchored reform momentum.

outlook_next_decade: Prospects depend more on politics than macroeconomics: low debt and a credible currency board are strengths, but fragmented governance and slow reform constrain EU accession progress. Inflation should stay near euro-area levels given the peg. The upside is EU integration unlocking investment; the downside is political fragmentation or a slowdown in the EU, Bosnia's main trade partner, transmitting directly through the currency board.
